subject.title: Context pruning mode 'off' not preventing compactions (Anthropic API key, cache-ttl smart defaults)

question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit compaction hard-limit-only/off mode, or keep auto-compaction available and focus only on fixing false low-context triggers plus trigger metadata?
rationale: The bug portion is partly fixed on main, but the requested disable mode is a new config/safety contract that repository policy treats as product-sensitive.

options.title: Fix triggers first
options.body: Keep automatic compaction available, add trigger attribution, and only fix reproducible low-context accounting bugs before reconsidering a new mode.

options.title: Add explicit hard-limit mode
options.body: Introduce a documented config mode with migration/docs/tests that disables threshold compaction while preserving unavoidable overflow recovery.

options.title: Close after partial fix
options.body: Treat the Anthropic cached-usage fix and current docs as sufficient unless a current-main repro is posted.

recommendation.title: Fix triggers first
recommendation.body: Keep automatic compaction available, add trigger attribution, and only fix reproducible low-context accounting bugs before reconsidering a new mode.

likelyOwner.reason: This person is the best current-history routing candidate for the config/schema and compaction policy surface, though final product authority is not established by git history alone.
